abbott_smith_html:
δοκέω, -ῶ
(δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב, etc. ;]
__1. to be of opinion, suppose: Mat.24:44, Luk.12:40, Heb.10:29; with inf., Mat.3:9, Luk.8:18 24:37, Jhn.5:39 16:2, Act.12:9 27:13, 1Co.3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37, Gal.6:3, Php.3:4, Jas.1:26; with accusative and inf., 1Co.12:23, 2Co.11:16; before ὅτι, Mat.6:7 26:53, Mrk.6:49, Luk.12:51 13:2, 4 19:11, Jhn.5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15, 1Co.4:9, 2Co.12:19, Jas.4:5.
__2. to seem, be reputed: Act.25:27; with inf., Mrk.10:42, Luk.10:36 22:24, Act.17:13 26:9, 1Co.11:16 12:22, 2Co.10:9, Gal.2:6, 9, Heb.4:1 12:11; οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute, Gal.2:2. Impers., it seems, with dative of person(s);
__(a) to think: Mat.17:25 18:12 21:28 22:17, 42 26:66, Jhn.11:56, Heb.12:10;
__(b) to please, seem good to: with inf., Luk.1:3, Act.15:22, 25 15:23, 34.†
SYN. (δοκέω 1): ἡγέομαι 2, νομίζω2, οἴομαι; ἡ. and ν. properly express belief resting on external proof, ἡ. denoting the more careful judgment; δ. and οἴ. imply a subjective judgment which in the case of οἴ. is based on feeling, in δ. on thought (see Schmidt, with 17) (δοκέω2): φαίνομαι; φ., from the standpoint of the object, "expresses how a matter phenomenally shows and presents itself"; δ., from the standpoint of the observer, expresses one's subjective judgment about a matter (see Tr., Syn., LXXx; Cremer, 204). (AS)

strongs_1890.strongs_def: compare the base of G1166 (δεικνύω)) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly)
strongs_1890.derivation: a prolonged form of a primary verb, (used only in an alternate in certain tenses;
strongs_1890.kjv_def: be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow

occurrences.bsb: And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
occurrences.kjv: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

occurrences.bsb: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
occurrences.kjv: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

occurrences.bsb: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”
occurrences.kjv: He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers?

occurrences.bsb: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
occurrences.kjv: How think ye? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and goeth into the mountains, and seeketh that which is gone astray?

occurrences.bsb: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’
occurrences.kjv: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.

occurrences.bsb: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
occurrences.kjv: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?

occurrences.bsb: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” “David’s,” they answered.
occurrences.kjv: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David.

occurrences.bsb: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
occurrences.kjv: Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.

occurrences.bsb: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
occurrences.kjv: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?

occurrences.bsb: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.
occurrences.kjv: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.

occurrences.bsb: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—
occurrences.kjv: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:

occurrences.bsb: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
occurrences.kjv: But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.

occurrences.bsb: Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,
occurrences.kjv: It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,

occurrences.bsb: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”
occurrences.kjv: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.

occurrences.bsb: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
occurrences.kjv: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?

occurrences.bsb: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
occurrences.kjv: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

occurrences.bsb: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
occurrences.kjv: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

occurrences.bsb: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?
occurrences.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?

occurrences.bsb: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
occurrences.kjv: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

occurrences.bsb: While the people were listening to this, Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.
occurrences.kjv: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.

occurrences.bsb: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them should be considered the greatest.
occurrences.kjv: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.

occurrences.bsb: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.
occurrences.kjv: But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

occurrences.bsb: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,
occurrences.kjv: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

occurrences.bsb: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
occurrences.kjv: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.

occurrences.bsb: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.
occurrences.kjv: Howbeit Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep.

occurrences.bsb: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.
occurrences.kjv: The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave to weep there.

occurrences.bsb: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”
occurrences.kjv: Then sought they for Jesus, and spake among themselves, as they stood in the temple, What think ye, that he will not come to the feast?

occurrences.bsb: Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
occurrences.kjv: For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.

occurrences.bsb: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
occurrences.kjv: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.

occurrences.bsb: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”
occurrences.kjv: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

occurrences.bsb: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
occurrences.kjv: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.

occurrences.bsb: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,
occurrences.kjv: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:

occurrences.bsb: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
occurrences.kjv: It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

occurrences.bsb: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
occurrences.kjv: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;

occurrences.bsb: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
occurrences.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.

occurrences.bsb: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
occurrences.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

occurrences.bsb: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
occurrences.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

occurrences.bsb: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
occurrences.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

occurrences.bsb: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
occurrences.kjv: Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seemeth to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise.

occurrences.bsb: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.
occurrences.kjv: For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.

occurrences.bsb: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
occurrences.kjv: But she is happier if she so abide, after my judgment: and I think also that I have the Spirit of God.

occurrences.bsb: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
occurrences.kjv: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.

occurrences.bsb: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
occurrences.kjv: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.

occurrences.bsb: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.
occurrences.kjv: But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.

occurrences.bsb: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
occurrences.kjv: Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary:

occurrences.bsb: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,
occurrences.kjv: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.

occurrences.bsb: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.
occurrences.kjv: If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.

occurrences.bsb: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
occurrences.kjv: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.

occurrences.bsb: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
occurrences.kjv: I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.

occurrences.bsb: Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.
occurrences.kjv: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

occurrences.bsb: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
occurrences.kjv: And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.

occurrences.bsb: But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism—those leaders added nothing to me.
occurrences.kjv: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:

occurrences.bsb: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
occurrences.kjv: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

occurrences.bsb: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
occurrences.kjv: For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

occurrences.bsb: though I myself could have such confidence. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more:
occurrences.kjv: Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinketh that he hath whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more:

occurrences.bsb: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.
occurrences.kjv: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.

occurrences.bsb: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
occurrences.kjv: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?

occurrences.bsb: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.
occurrences.kjv: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.

occurrences.bsb: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.
occurrences.kjv: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

occurrences.bsb: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
occurrences.kjv: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

occurrences.bsb: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
occurrences.kjv: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?
